title: Integrating Inverse Functions
author: DkfTkX7xNnbzLCF2p
chapter_outcomes: Integrate hyperbolic functions and recognise integrals of functions of the form $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{(a^2 - x^2)}}$, $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{(x^2 + a^2)}}$ and $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{(x^2 - a^2)}}$, and integrate associated functions using trigonometric or hyperbolic substitutions as appropriate
Derive and use reduction formulae for the evaluation of definite integrals

Understand how the area under a curve may be approximated by areas of rectangles, and use rectangles to estimate or set bounds for the area under a curve or to derive inequalities or limits concerning sums

Use integration to find arc lengths for curves with equations in Cartesian coordinates, including the use of a parameter, or in polar coordinates, and surface areas of revolution about one of the axes for curves with equations in Cartesian coordinates, including the use of a parameter.
